tokens: sessionStorage['ibsession'].sessionid — session ID (hex-like, ~40 chars) embedded inside JSON; set/updated early in session and appears stable afterward.
sessionStorage['u_scsid'] — opaque session/correlation token (~96 chars base64url-ish); written once on page load; no observed rotation in sampled events.
sessionStorage['u_scsid_r'] — same opaque token as u_scsid (~96 chars); added and later re-added/updated in session (suggests refresh/replication behavior).
data_blocks: sessionStorage['ibmappings'] — large JSON config/mappings blob (~10KB) containing payment/validation/config data (e.g., credit-card-prefixes, cvv-length, content-path, etc.).
sessionStorage['d_failedBeacon'] — very large JSON payload (~200KB+) containing serialized “patch”/DOM/style data for a failed telemetry/beacon retry queue (likely analytics/monitoring).
narrative: Capture is from https://www.amtrak.com. No clear first-party auth JWT/access_token/refresh_token or XSRF cookie was found in storage/window props from the sampled high-signal keys. The only clear token-like material is an internal session identifier stored in sessionStorage under 'ibsession' (as JSON with a 'sessionid' field) plus two opaque identifiers (u_scsid / u_scsid_r) that were flagged by keyword searches as potentially JWT-related but are actually opaque strings (no 3-part JWT structure). Storage is dominated by analytics/telemetry and tracking artifacts (Adobe 's_*' fields like s_pec ActivityMap clickstream, Branch session keys, etc.), which account for nearly all events. Meaningful non-token data includes a sizable 'ibmappings' configuration blob (likely used by booking/payment flows) and an unusually large 'd_failedBeacon' retry queue payload.
